items.title: Nat Hentoff interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: Dave Douglas is a man of great capacities but he has so many different combos.

ctx.x: Yeah, that’s a tough question. So do you think the future for jazz music is healthy? Is it possible to say that?

My main hope is that out of all — and I never anticipated there could be so much emphasis on education. I’m not talking about how to play, you know like the Berklee School of Music. I don’t know if I mentioned this in this interview, I was talking about it downstairs. There’s a place called North Texas State college, they have I don’t know how many big bands, all kinds of small combos. There’s one thing missing. And Benny Carter went there after I did and when I asked Benny what he thought he said, “gee they…
It’s not swinging, ey? I often see the phrase jazz, America’s only true art form.

items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Meanwhile Stanley, a black writer, throws one brick at Dave Douglas, a white trumpet player, and not even that much of a brick. And he is right.

ctx.x: Although I’ve changed my view of Wynton.
Okay, wait. I’m going somewhere else. Meanwhile Stanley, a black writer, throws one brick at Dave Douglas, a white trumpet player, and not even that much of a brick.
